Content:
One way to find the determinant of a [MATH: 3\!\times\! 3] matrix [MATH: A] is to take the alternating sum of the entries of the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:
[MATH: \det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}M_{11}} - {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}M_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}M_{13}}]

Content:
Remember that we had to change the sign of the second product. When we multiply a minor of an entry by the respective sign in the formula like this, we get the cofactor of the entry. The cofactors in the above formula were [MATH: {\color{blue}M_{11}},] [MATH: -{\color{blue}M_{12}},] and [MATH: {\color{blue}M_{13}}.]

Content:
Using this idea, we can write the formula for the determinant of a [MATH: 3\!\times\! 3] matrix [MATH: A] in terms of cofactors, as follows:
[MATH: \det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}C_{11}} + {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}C_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}C_{13}}]

Content:
This is called the cofactor expansion of the determinant across the first row.

Content:
In fact, we can use a similar method of multiplying the entries of the top row of the matrix by their respective cofactors to find the determinant for any [MATH: n\!\times\! n] matrix [MATH: A] when [MATH: n>3]. The formula is
[MATH: det(A)|= ∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{1j}C_{1j}; = a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + ⋯ + a_{1n}C_{1n}.]

Content:
Let's see how to use this formula in the next example.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The minor of the entry [MATH: a_{ij}] in a [MATH: n\times n] matrix is the determinant that we get when the rows and columns containing [MATH: a_{ij}] are removed.

Content:
For example, suppose that we wish to find the minor of [MATH: a_{32}] in the following matrix:
[MATH: [2|3|2|3; 4|2|5|12; 1|− 2|0|− 5; − 5|1|3|0]]

Content:
To get the minor of [MATH: a_{\color{red}{3}\color{blue}{2}}], we remove the [MATH: \color{red}3]rd row and [MATH: \color{blue}2]nd column:

Content:
[MATH: [2|∗|2|3; 4|∗|5|12; ∗|− 2|∗|∗; − 5|∗|3|0]]

Content:
So, the minor of [MATH: a_{32}], denoted [MATH: M_{32}], is

Content:
[MATH: |2|2|3; 4|5|12; − 5|3|0|]

Content:
We can now calculate the value of [MATH: M_{32}] by evaluating the determinant using previously discussed methods.

---

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To get the minor of [MATH: a_{13}], we remove the [MATH: 1]st row and [MATH: 3]rd column:

[MATH: [∗|∗|2|∗; 5|1|∗|0; 1|6|∗|− 1; − 6|3|∗|0]]

So, the minor is

Item 9 — Tutorial: Calculating Determinants Using Cofactors

Content:
One way to find the determinant of a [MATH: 3\!\times\! 3] matrix [MATH: A] is to take the alternating sum of the entries of the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:
[MATH: \det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}M_{11}} - {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}M_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}M_{13}}]

Content:
Remember that we had to change the sign of the second product. When we multiply a minor of an entry by the respective sign in the formula like this, we get the cofactor of the entry. The cofactors in the above formula were [MATH: {\color{blue}M_{11}},] [MATH: -{\color{blue}M_{12}},] and [MATH: {\color{blue}M_{13}}.]

Content:
Using this idea, we can write the formula for the determinant of a [MATH: 3\!\times\! 3] matrix [MATH: A] in terms of cofactors, as follows:
[MATH: \det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}C_{11}} + {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}C_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}C_{13}}]

Content:
This is called the cofactor expansion of the determinant across the first row.

Content:
In fact, we can use a similar method of multiplying the entries of the top row of the matrix by their respective cofactors to find the determinant for any [MATH: n\!\times\! n] matrix [MATH: A] when [MATH: n>3]. The formula is
[MATH: det(A)|= ∑_(j = 1)^(n)a_{1j}C_{1j}; = a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + ⋯ + a_{1n}C_{1n}.]

Content:
Let's see how to use this formula in the next example.

---

Item 10 — Example: Calculating the Determinant of a NxN Matrix Using Cofactor Expansion

Example Prompt:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
[MATH: 0|0|2|0; 5|1|2|0; 1|6|0|− 1; − 6|3|1|0]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

[MATH: det(A)|= a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + a_{13}C_{13} + a_{14}C_{14}; = 0 ⋅ C_{11} + 0 ⋅ C_{12} + 2 ⋅ C_{13} + 0 ⋅ C_{14}; = 2C_{13}; = 2 ⋅|∗|∗|2|∗; 5|1|∗|0; 1|6|∗|− 1; − 6|3|∗|0|; = 2(− 1)^{1 + 3}|5|1|0; 1|6|− 1; − 6|3|0|; = 2(5|6|− 1; 3|0|− 1|1|− 1; − 6|0|+ 0|1|6; − 6|3|); = 2(5(6 ⋅ 0 + 1 ⋅ 3) − (1 ⋅ 0 − (− 1) ⋅ (− 6)) + 0(1 ⋅ 3 − 6 ⋅ (− 6))); = 2(15 + 6 + 0); = 2 ⋅ 21; = 42]
